tools.description: Use to build a list from a shape: size, location, industry, technology. It bills per page, so ask for the page size you need rather than paging through the whole market.
Enrich up to ten companies in one call, billed 30 Firecrawl credits per matched company; unmatched records are free.
Use when you have a domain or LinkedIn company URL and need the company behind it. For a company you can only name, search first.

Call first when starting from a company name or ticker: it returns every other identifier, so one call here makes the rest of this provider addressable. Also the only place peers and secondary listings are published.
Look up a company by its Apollo ID; use companies/enrich when you have a domain instead.
To resolve an employer slug (the segment after join.com/companies/) to its numeric company id and city ids before listing jobs, or to read the employer's benefits and offices.

Call to discover what is covered, or to resolve names to identifiers when you do not already have a ticker. Check the per-company dataset list before assuming a costlier capability will answer for it.

Call for the current standing position of officers and directors, including holdings held through trusts and other vehicles. Use insider-transactions for what they have been doing rather than what they hold.
Call to find which companies professional investors are actually writing about, and how heavily, before asking what they said.

Call for the qualitative case on a company as professional investors put it, with the stance and conviction attached. The one capability here that answers what people think rather than what was reported.

Read video metadata, description and any available transcript. Transcript availability is not guaranteed. Not channel listings, comments or timestamped captions. Scrape pricing per successful attempt: 1 credit base, plus 4 for audio and 4 for video (5 for either, 9 for both), before other Scrape surcharges. The wrapper adds no charge; underlying Scrape requests are billed separately at their current rate. Invalid YouTube Markdown may trigger one fresh Scrape call.
